# California Rent-Increase Notice Review

A written rent-increase notice during a fixed-term lease can be confusing, especially when the lease still has months left. The safest next step is to verify the notice against your lease, your payment history, and any local rules that may apply.

## Tenant Checklist for Reviewing the Notice

- **Read the lease first**
  - Check the lease end date: **2026-10-31**
  - Look for clauses about:
    - rent increases during the lease term
    - notice requirements
    - renewal or month-to-month conversion
    - addenda or amendments

- **Check the notice details**
  - Date received: **2026-03-05**
  - Increase effective date: **2026-04-01**
  - Increase amount: **12%**
  - Confirm whether the notice identifies:
    - the current rent
    - the new rent amount
    - the date the change starts
    - who sent it and how it was delivered

- **Compare the timeline**
  - Your lease still runs until **2026-10-31**
  - Ask whether the landlord is treating the tenancy as:
    - fixed-term lease
    - renewal offer
    - month-to-month arrangement
    - separate written amendment

- **Check local rent rules**
  - California has state and local rules that can affect rent increases, notice periods, and lease protections.
  - If your city has rent control or tenant protections, those may matter.

- **Keep your payment record current**
  - Continue paying rent on time while you clarify the notice unless you receive different written instructions.
  - Keep proof of every payment.

## Documents to Gather

- Signed lease and all addenda
- The rent-increase notice
- Any renewal offers or lease modification letters
- Rent payment records, receipts, bank statements, or portal screenshots
- Email, text, or letter communications with the landlord
- Move-in paperwork and any prior notices about rent changes
- Any local tenant handbook, rent board notice, or city ordinance summary if you have one

## Questions to Ask the Landlord

- “My lease ends on **2026-10-31**. Does this notice apply during the current fixed term, or is it intended for a renewal period?”
- “What lease clause or agreement supports the increase effective **2026-04-01**?”
- “What will my new monthly rent be in dollars?”
- “Is this notice meant as a proposal, a renewal term, or a formal amendment?”
- “Does this notice comply with the required notice period under my lease and local rules?”
- “Should I sign anything, or is this simply informational?”
- “If I do not agree, what is the landlord’s next step?”

## Calm Response You Can Send

**Subject:** Request for clarification about rent notice

Hello [Landlord Name],

I received your written notice dated **2026-03-05** stating that rent will increase by **12%** effective **2026-04-01**. My current lease term runs through **2026-10-31**, so I would like to confirm how this notice applies to my tenancy.

Could you please clarify:
- whether this increase is intended to apply during the current lease term or at renewal
- the exact new monthly rent amount
- the lease clause or agreement supporting the change
- whether any document needs to be signed

Thank you for your help. I want to make sure I understand the notice correctly and keep my records accurate.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

## Practical Next Steps

- Save the notice and lease in one folder
- Write down the dates and amounts
- Send the clarification message in writing
- Keep paying rent on time unless you receive a different written instruction
- If the response is unclear, consider contacting a local tenant resource or legal aid organization for general guidance

## Sources

- California Civil Code overview: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=827.&lawCode=CIV
- California Department of Consumer Affairs tenant resources: https://www.dca.ca.gov/publications/landlordbook/tenant.shtml
- California Courts self-help housing information: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/housing-problems
